races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden

runners_data.name: Brigerbad
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan runner returning after 32 days; recorded a solo start finishing last over 6f on good — a natural hold-up operator whose deeper finishing tendencies and single poor run make it hard to construct a compelling case at this trip on yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Camino Lad
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for G M Lyons on this lightly-raced three-year-old who has placed twice from three starts — step back to 8f from 10f and 12f attempts looks a more sensible pitch, and his tactical flexibility gives Keane options to sit prominently if the tempo allows.

runners_data.name: Caption This
runners_data.note: Robbie Colgan and J A Nash combine on this complete debutant with no form to assess and an UNKNOWN going profile — lightly raced flag applies, making this a genuinely open unknown, though Nash/Colgan is a live combination for a well-prepared first-timer.

runners_data.name: Karrygrant
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner for J P Murtagh; Ben Coen has ridden him to four placed efforts from eight starts and knows his rhythm well — on yielding ground with no pace rival, he controls the race completely, though the style-fit tag signals he is stretched by conditions here and rivals may get at him late.

runners_data.name: Willofthepeople
runners_data.note: Back after a lengthy 319-day absence for G M Lyons wearing a tongue-tie, with a modest form string of 4-0-8 over shorter trips — the long layoff and question marks over stamina at a mile on yielding ground are significant barriers, and the hold-up profile means he races towards midfield against preference in this shape.

runners_data.name: Misneach Sile
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's runner with Jack Cleary (5lb claim) in the saddle; returned a 12th on debut over 8f and is a natural closer asked to function further forward than ideal here, with the going experience limited to one run — the apprentice claim partially offsets the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Mosel
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle gives this Joseph O'Brien-trained colt strong pilot credentials after a single seventh on debut over 9f on good — pedigree and stable suggest significant improvement is possible, and DBM's ability to find a run from midfield makes this one of the more interesting hold-up profiles in the field despite the redistribution.

runners_data.name: Orphanina
runners_data.note: Conor David Maxwell-trained filly with a single debut run (10th over 8f on good) and an unknown jockey/going combination on this occasion — lightly raced flag and fade-in-finish note combine to leave this on the periphery of interest unless her training form suggests something different.

runners_data.name: Peshwari Nan
runners_data.note: Back after a significant 179-day absence for John C McConnell with Nicola Burns claiming 5lb; both starts came on standard ground rather than yielding, flagging a genuine going concern, and the extended layoff adds another layer of uncertainty for a hold-up type who cannot get her natural position anyway.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's filly has run 11th, 11th and 14th in three outings on good ground — the form is deeply unencouraging regardless of positional factors, and the 7-day turnaround for a horse who has shown nothing suggests connections are simply gaining experience rather than attacking this.

runners_data.name: Star Of Beauty
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this K J Condon runner who has been placed four times including twice second, all on good ground at 8f — the most consistent form line in the race, the prominent style suits tracking Karrygrant perfectly, and the visor headgear adds a tactical edge, though the all-good-ground profile is worth watching on yielding.

runners_data.name: Sweetie Too
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary rides for Brendan Duke; two starts have produced an 8th and 10th over 8f on good, and the hold-up style combined with a fades-in-finish flag leaves little to commend despite the 22-day freshener — needs substantial improvement to threaten.

runners_data.name: Tax Me Later
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse rides this Daniel McLoughlin debutant with a completely unknown profile — no form, no going data, and an unknown style designation make assessment impossible, though a well-prepared first-timer from a yard that occasionally springs a surprise should never be entirely dismissed.

runners_data.name: Whatsin The Stars
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche partners this Paul Flynn runner who has finished 15th and 11th on both starts over 8f on good — the hold-up style is compromised by the redistribution, and consecutive tail-end finishes on similar going give little basis for optimism even with the tongue-tie applied.

runners_data.name: Wooloongabba
runners_data.note: Shane Foley is a booking that elevates interest slightly for John C McConnell's runner, but an 11th and 13th over shorter trips on good ground — combined with the natural closer profile displaced from its preferred position — means the talented jockey faces an uphill task against more exposed rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Karrygrant is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner maiden, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Ben Coen's mount will be able to control the tempo from the front at whatever pace suits — on yielding ground over a mile at Bellewstown, that figures to be a measured, energy-conserving gallop rather than a lung-bursting sprint. Star Of Beauty is the most likely horse to press or track Karrygrant prominently, with Camino Lad also capable of landing a handy position if connections choose to deploy him forward. The field contains substantially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Peshwari Nan, Mosel, Misneach Sile, Brigerbad, and others are genuine closers who will all be competing for the same ground in midfield and behind, meaning several race out of their preferred position and their finishing kicks may cancel each other out. This race shape — a lone leader on a fair pace, small finish-line surge on soft-ish ground — strongly favours runners who can track prominently in the slipstream and pounce inside the final two furlongs, rather than hold-up horses trying to weave through a congested pack late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Karrygrant Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Karrygrant is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a comfortable, controlled tempo that no rival is able to interrupt.
scenarios.body: Ben Coen dictates every yard on yielding ground, the pace is fair but never fierce, and the race fails to develop a strong finishing burst — Karrygrant's stamina and tactical supremacy keep him in front into the final furlong. Prominent trackers who can muster a sustained challenge rather than a late sprint are the danger, as the tempo never truly tests those held up deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the close-tracking horses swoops past Karrygrant inside the final two furlongs as the leader's stamina is tested on yielding ground.
scenarios.body: Karrygrant sets the race up perfectly but the sustained effort in yielding conditions takes its toll in the closing stages, and a horse who has been sitting a length or two off the pace throughout picks up most cleanly. Star Of Beauty, with multiple placed efforts at the trip on good ground and a prominent style, is ideally suited to this unfolding.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the field strings out, creating a gap for one of the better-credentialled closers to thread through in the straight.
scenarios.body: Even though most hold-up types are mapped to midfield against their preference, a genuine acceleration mid-race could clear a lane for one to deliver a late surge — Mosel, trained by Joseph O'Brien with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard, carries most raw potential upside here. Brigerbad under Siobhan Rutledge also fits the profile but carries a fades-in-finish flag that tempers expectation materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners ignore roles and push forward, creating an unexpectedly hot early gallop that burns out the pace-setters and leaves the race wide open.
scenarios.body: Should the opening quarter-mile become ragged and competitive, the resulting strong pace on yielding ground sets up a messy, scrambling finish where stamina and luck in running matter more than tactical position. This is the least likely shape given only Karrygrant is a confirmed pace-maker, but a chaotic scenario could gift an opportunity to an unexposed debutant like Caption This or Tax Me Later.

watchPoints.text: Karrygrant with Ben Coen sets the race's entire shape — watch whether he is allowed a genuine lead from the outset or if any rival attempts to hassle him into the first bend, as that determines pace classification and which profiles are activated.

Star Of Beauty's going record is exclusively on good ground and today's conditions are yielding — if she shows any discomfort in the early stages tracking Karrygrant, the most obvious prominent challenger is removed from the picture.

Mosel with Dylan Browne McMonagle is the hold-up horse most likely to find an unconventional run through the field — watch for DBM positioning him on the outside of the midfield pack rather than accepting a deep draw, as an unobstructed run to the rail in the straight changes this runner's prospects materially.

The cluster of John C McConnell runners (Misneach Sile, Peshwari Nan, Wooloongabba) creates potential stable-mate traffic in midfield — all three are natural closers mapped toward midfield, and their proximity could result in interference or blocked runs that affect each other's finishing effort.

Caption This and Tax Me Later are complete debutants with unknown styles — if either breaks sharply and slots prominently behind Karrygrant, the positional map changes for every other prominent-seeking runner in the race.

races.name: Ploughman Bar & Grill Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field and likely to stride to the front uncontested; good trainer strike rate concern noted with Hughes at 0/4 over 14 days, but Colin Keane's presence is a significant positive and yielding ground is within his comfort range based on 12 of 14 similar-going runs suggesting adaptability.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but finished seventh last time out, which tempers enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and 140 lb is a stiff ask off an official mark of 57.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a modest recent record — nine runs without a win or place — and though yielding ground is within her profile, she has shown little on similar surfaces and faces a difficult task finding her way through a tightly-packed field from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Suerte nevertheless has experience over today's trip and comes here fresh enough on a 19-day turnaround, though she carries 139 lb from stall 12 and her recent string of unplaced efforts makes improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Wegotogether
runners_data.note: Has been off for 101 days which is a notable absence concern, races held-up, and has previously been placed on similar ground; Gary Carroll rides and Gavin Cromwell's yard has been active (7/27 over 14 days), but this is his first try at the mile trip.
runners_data.comment: Wegotogether has run over today's trip and going, and with her trainer striking at 26% in the last fortnight she arrives with strong support behind her; the concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts and returns after 101 days off.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant liability on yielding ground over a mile; ran well in January (won at 7f on Soft) but recent form reads poorly and the hold-up style with a tendency to fade makes her hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Wellwhatshappenin arrives 19 days fresh after back-to-back unplaced efforts, yet he showed better form deeper in the sequence with a third three starts back and a winner five starts back, giving him something to build on; 139 lb from stall 13 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Distillate
runners_data.note: 148 days off the track is a major fitness query; hold-up horse who has shown a place at 7f on similar ground but is returning from a long absence for Adrian McGuinness and will need significant improvement to factor from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Distillate has experience over today's trip and going, and her second four starts back gives her a profile worth respecting, with our rating of 58 suggesting she holds claims in this field; the main worry is a 148-day absence coupled with three winless outings in her most recent starts.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader over the shorter distances he has been running — stepping up to a mile here but a record of 800008 does not inspire confidence; Denis Hogan yard has had some activity (2/22 over 14 days) and the hold-up style leaves him needing luck in running.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Heart Of Eternity heads here just nine days after her latest eighth-place effort, and while she has run over today's trip and carries a manageable 135 lb from stall six, her persistent struggles for form make her hard to fancy from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a fade flag and a very limited form sample of just three runs, all on Good ground; Ben Coen takes the ride which is an upgrade in quality, but the horse drops back from 12f and has not shown enough to suggest he can maintain a prominent position through a testing mile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with back-to-back ninths the most recent evidence, Pettus Bridge faces a stiff ask from stall 16 carrying 131 lb, and a rating of 36 ranked last of 16 leaves little to cling to, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by nature, though the crowded hold-up pool means he is likely to end up in midfield rather than his natural position at the rear; six runs without a win or place, and form of 000008 offers little encouragement regardless of where he settles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lohengrin does at least bring distance experience to the table and is fit enough having run just 13 days ago, though a top-speed figure of 60 and an official mark of 45 suggest he faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Has a win on Soft ground at 8f in his history and two placed runs at the trip, making him one of the more credible hold-up types in the field; Wayne Lordan is a top booking and while he is redistributed toward midfield, his form profile is among the strongest of the hold-up group if he can find a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 16 on our figures and officially rated just 43, Draiocht is hard to fancy against this field, though he does bring distance and going experience and returns on a fresh enough 19-day break, with a third last time out at least showing some recent consistency.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Holds a recent 4th at 8f on Good ground and a 5th on Good over 10f, suggesting the mile is within his range; a genuine hold-up horse pushed toward midfield by the volume of similar types, but James Ryan is capable of finding a route through if the race opens up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, La Campanella arrives here on a sharp 13-day turnaround with experience over today's trip in her favour, though a fourth two starts back is the best she has offered recently, and a rating of 43 suggests she faces a stiff ask from stall four carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse who has been running consistently without ever threatening to win — 670078 recent form on similar ground — and a 7-year-old handicapper who has found his level; Sadhbh Tormey rides with a 7lb claim which helps the weight but the form says little.
runners_data.comment: Rampage has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 58 places him third among 16 runners, suggesting he holds genuine claims here; the concern is a winless recent sequence in his last six starts that makes the case harder to seal.

runners_data.name: Tullyesker
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade flag and a limited record of just four runs — the most recent two on Soft and Yielding ground where he finished 8th both times; redistributed to midfield because of the density of hold-up types, and the tendency to fade makes a strong finish unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Tullyesker has been winless in his last four starts, finishing eighth twice and unplaced twice, and a rating of 43 ranked twelfth of sixteen makes him hard to fancy; the 55-day absence is a concern, though he has run over today's trip and draws stall one.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Has been running over 13-14f and drops sharply in trip to a mile here, which looks a significant concern — recent form includes plenty of zeros; true hold-up horse pushed toward midfield and the combination of trip drop, fade flag, and poor recent form makes this a very tough task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 15 of 16 on our figures, Bang Po makes little appeal, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns from a 54-day break with a handy draw in stall two.

runners_data.name: Hale Bopp
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran whose best recent effort was a 3rd at 8f on Good ground; true hold-up horse who will be in the vicinity of midfield in practice, and while Sweeney's yard is light on recent runners, the horse has placed on similar ground within the last five runs.
runners_data.comment: Hale Bopp arrives winless in recent starts and returns after a 75-day absence, which raises a fitness query, though he has experience over today's trip and going; a third three starts back offers some encouragement, but two unplaced efforts since then keep him a tentative proposition from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: Fade flag is notable for an eight-year-old hold-up horse who has been running over 9-10f; stepping back to a mile and drawn into a crowded rear-of-field group, Shane Foley is the strongest jockey booking of the hold-up brigade and could navigate traffic, but form offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-field and unplaced efforts, Jazz Dreamers is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked 14 of 16 — though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 31-day break.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent horse who has five top-seven finishes in his last five runs at 7-8f on Good ground, all at similar distances; a 10-year-old veteran who knows his job and with Reserve 1 likely to be a competent booking, his ability to travel close to Launch Time makes him tactically well-placed for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Brains has been winless in his last six starts, though a second six starts back hints at better days, and he arrives fit on a quick turnaround five days ago; experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 62 that tops the field, makes him the one to beat here.

races.paceDynamic: Launch Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse field and is expected to stride to the front unchallenged, dictating a steady, sustainable gallop on yielding ground at Bellewstown. Rampage and Pettus Bridge are the only other prominent-style horses, but neither carries the profile or form to seriously contest the lead, meaning Launch Time can control fractions without burning energy. With the pace honest but uncontested, horses racing close to the leader in the first three or four positions will travel in the slipstream without being asked early questions — a significant positional advantage on ground that will drain late stamina. This race shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can enjoy a clean trip and pounce from a position of cover, rather than true hold-up horses who must navigate traffic and find their finishing kick from deep. Several horses tagged as redistributed — including Lohengrin, Draiocht, La Campanella, Tullyesker, Bang Po, Hale Bopp and Jazz Dreamers — are genuine hold-up types who cannot all settle at the rear as they would wish; of these, Draiocht and La Campanella appear best placed to push wider and secure a more forward berth than the map indicates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Launch Time Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time leads at a steady clip on yielding ground and the field strings out behind, allowing prominent horses to travel comfortably in his wake.
scenarios.body: Launch Time dictates every fraction without pressure, and horses able to track him within the first four positions will arrive at the two-furlong marker full of running; prominent types who stay close enough to pounce when the pace lifts entering the straight will be hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Sprint Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely modest and runners in second to fourth place sprint for home early in the straight, catching hold-up horses flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace on yielding ground compresses the field and creates a sprint-style finish that rewards horses with tactical speed and a prominent pitch; hold-up horses redistributed to midfield will have too much ground to make up and suffer interference in traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time's pace is faster than expected and the field opens up enough for genuine hold-up horses to find a clear run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: An honest gallop on yielding ground will drain the leaders' reserves late, theoretically giving hold-up horses a platform to close — but with so many redistributed types unable to find their natural rear-of-field position, only those who genuinely secure a clean passage will benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 16 causes significant interference, false positions, and several hold-up horses are forced wider or checked, scrambling the finish entirely.
scenarios.body: Traffic problems in a 16-runner field on a sharp Bellewstown circuit create openings for horses with tactical versatility and jockey quality to exploit gaps; the compressed mid-race shape punishes any horse that loses momentum in running.

watchPoints.text: Launch Time (Colin Keane) is the lone confirmed pace-setter — if he is allowed to stride to the front unopposed and sets a sustainable clip, the first few positions directly behind him become the prime real estate in this race and must be monitored at the start.

The 16-runner field contains at least seven genuine hold-up horses unable to secure their natural position at the rear — watch the first two furlongs for significant jostling and potential interference as Lohengrin, Draiocht, La Campanella, Tullyesker, Bang Po, Hale Bopp and Jazz Dreamers all compete for space in midfield.

Pettus Bridge (Ben Coen) has a fade flag and is dropping back from 12f — if Coen attempts to push forward prominently to exploit a near-empty early position, he could take on Launch Time and compress the pace earlier than expected, changing the race shape significantly.

Draiocht (Wayne Lordan) is the hold-up horse with the best form claim in this field and has a win on Soft at 8f — watch where Lordan positions him in the first half mile, as a wide-angled run into the straight could be his route to a competitive finish if the pace is honest.

Brains is the most consistent horse in the race on paper and races prominently — with Reserve 1 in the saddle, watch whether he can tuck in directly behind Launch Time and travel for free before making his challenge entering the final two furlongs.

races.name: Ploughman Bar & Grill Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Albion Power
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose recent form reads poorly — four finishes of 9th or worse — and who has no wins or placings on similar going in five relevant runs; Colin McAteer's mount needs more pace than this race will generate to close into contention.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Albion Power did finish fourth three starts back and shaped with some promise, while experience over today's trip and a rating of 64 on our figures offer encouragement; sixty days off the track is the main query.

runners_data.name: Givehertilxmas
runners_data.note: Colin Keane booking for a Gerard Keane-trained 4yo is the key angle here; the hold-up style suits a tracking position if she can get it, placed twice on good ground, but 56 days off and a tongue-tie to note.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Givehertilxmas at least showed a return to form with a third last time out, though a 56-day absence and 142 lb from stall 15 are factors to weigh against her having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with two wins and six places from 14 similar-going runs — outstanding ground fit — who is in reality a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the rear is overcrowded; his 9-day turnaround is fresh enough and the going is firmly in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Dinamine showed he can win when landing a success three starts back, but has been unplaced last time out and found little in between, leaving his current form patchy; he has run over today's trip and going, though his rating of 54 gives him plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Tracked prominently in a strong staying handicap last time out and finished second over 10f on good ground; Denis Hogan's 4yo handles this trip and surface, and a tongue-tie plus the blinker entry is worth noting as a first-time headgear angle.
runners_data.comment: Medieval Night has shown he can mix it at this level, finishing second last time out and third in his last six, though a sixth and seventh in between highlight his inconsistency; yet to win in recent starts, he has distance and going experience to call on, but 141 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 10f on good ground and handles the 8f trip; hold-up style should sit comfortably in mid-to-rear, and the consistent position-three finishes suggest a horse who runs his race without being pace-dependent, though Ronan Whelan will need to find room.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Judgement ran a fine second last time out and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going on his side; ranked top of the field on our ratings, the chief risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter; Adrian McGuinness's 4yo won at 8f on good ground and goes fresh after 13 days, but a STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) warns he is unlikely to fully dominate from the front in a field this competitive — Adam Caffrey will need to dictate cleanly to make his lead count.
runners_data.comment: Land Of The Giants shaped with promise when third four starts back and arrives here fit on a 13-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and a rating of 63 lending him strong claims; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from a latest fourth.

runners_data.name: Think About It
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant jockey booking for a lightly-raced 4yo who has shown ability at this trip on soft ground; his natural home is at the rear but the overcrowded hold-up division forces him into a midfield role, and his best form came over further.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Think About It heads here 20 days after her latest unplaced effort, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, her recent record offers little encouragement; a rating of 55 in a 15-runner field leaves her with plenty to prove from stall 8 carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Bright Dick
runners_data.note: Returning from a remarkable 775-day absence for Luke Comer; he showed prominent-tracking ability with a third over 9f and carries a tongue-tie, but the length of break makes fitness the overriding concern regardless of style.
runners_data.comment: Bright Dick shaped with promise when third in his most recent start, and has run over today's distance and going, giving him obvious claims here; the significant concern is a 775-day absence, which makes his fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on good ground and finished second at the same trip — the form is relevant — and Seamie Heffernan's presence on a 4yo for Donal Kinsella is a clear confidence signal; a genuine hold-up horse repositioned to midfield on the map, so Heffernan's ability to find clear running becomes critical.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in each of his last two starts, Micasso has been out of the frame more often than not in recent outings and, ranked eleventh of fifteen on our figures, he faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Oitentinha
runners_data.note: Tagged as a hold-up type who fades in the finish, repositioned to midfield on the map from her natural rear position; the five soft-ground runs show a pattern of finishing in the 8th-12th bracket, and 67 days off adds a fitness query.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 67 days off, Oitentinha faces questions about form, though she has run over today's distance and going and a step up from her official mark to a speed rating of 65 offers a sliver of encouragement from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Chant d'Or
runners_data.note: 308 days absent, only three career runs, and a headgear (blinkers) flag; a fader in the finish who would naturally race from the rear, the lengthy layoff and limited experience make this a significant risk even before the race-shape analysis.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after 308 days off, Chant d'Or faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures, and a trainer without a winner in 20 recent attempts does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Sunday Sovereign
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has shown ability at this trip in a 3rd-place finish on soft ground, but a prominent style combined with a fades-in-finish tag and 81 days absent make this hard to recommend; Zoe McMullan (10lb claimer) could aid the weight allowance.
runners_data.comment: Sunday Sovereign arrives 81 days since his last outing and is yet to win in recent starts, with a third three starts back the sole encouragement in a largely modest recent sequence; 127 lb from stall 12 adds to the challenge, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on Denise Foster's 5yo who finished 2nd and 4th in recent outings at 10f on good ground; her natural hold-up style is squeezed into midfield on the map, and the step back to 8f from 10f is a minor concern given her form has come over a longer trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 15 on our figures, Duchess Anne faces a stiff task from stall 11 off a mark of 43, though a runner-up finish last time out and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Finished 3rd over 10f on good ground and 5th over 9f — the trip is on the shorter side; Declan McDonogh's booking is a positive, and he has relevant soft-ground form, but he's a hold-up horse mapped to midfield by necessity with the style-fit discount applying.
runners_data.comment: Master Garvey arrives on the back of a seventh and ninth in his last two starts, and while he did show a third three starts back, he is winless in recent starts and ranks thirteenth of fifteen on our figures, making him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Monzoon
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old with a 256-day break, a series of double-figure finishes on similar ground, and a fades-in-the-finish pattern; Sadhbh Tormey (7lb claimer) cannot compensate for what the form record says, and this horse's natural rear position is already reassigned to midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 256 days, Monzoon is a tough sell here — ranked 14 of 15 on our figures — though he has run over today's distance and going before and carries a manageable 122 lb from stall three.

races.paceDynamic: Land Of The Giants is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner mile handicap at Bellewstown and, with no genuine pace rival to push him on, he is likely to control the tempo from the front at a comfortable, sustainable clip on yielding ground. Bright Dick and Sunday Sovereign offer some prominent interest but neither is a natural pace-forcing type, meaning Land Of The Giants should get a soft lead with minimal pressure. The yielding conditions at Bellewstown will slow the overall tempo further, compressing the field and reducing the benefit of sitting last — horses racing in midfield or handy to the pace will be best placed to exploit any late gaps. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can track through midfield and pounce in the straight, rather than true closers stuck wide at the rear, and prominent racers who can travel just behind the leader on a controlled tempo. The field contains far more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Dinamine, Think About It, Micasso, Duchess Anne, Master Garvey, Monzoon, Oitentinha and Chant d'Or are all genuine rear-of-field horses who cannot all get their natural position; of these, Dinamine (proven on good-to-soft, freshest on form) and Micasso (lowest mileage, class acts in behind) are most likely to secure a workable midfield berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants dictates a steady pace unchallenged and the winner comes from a prominent or tracking position.
scenarios.body: Land Of The Giants sets an uncontested gallop on yielding ground, the tempo is comfortable enough to keep the field strung out but not fast enough to stop the leader, and horses who track in second or third are perfectly poised to collar him late. Prominent types who handle the ground and stay the mile without needing a strong pace to run into are the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo proves too slow and a genuine hold-up horse threads through from midfield in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop on yielding ground leaves the pace horses treading water late, and a horse who has been quietly covered up tracking the midfield bunch suddenly finds daylight to sprint clear. Dinamine and Micasso, both redistributed from their natural rear position but with the class and going-form to capitalise, are the most dangerous in this shape if they secure a workable position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants kicks from the front at the two-furlong pole and the field fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: On a flat track with yielding ground slowing the closers' finishing kicks, Land Of The Giants sets an honest gallop then finds extra when challenged, and the big field leaves the hold-up horses with traffic to navigate too late. A front-runner who handles soft ground and is ridden with tactical confidence by Adam Caffrey would benefit most, with Bright Dick the most likely prominent threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Trouble, Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference in the straight and a horse who avoids trouble from an inside berth benefits.
scenarios.body: With 15 runners on a one-mile circuit and most of the field genuine hold-up types forced into tighter berths than ideal, the straight becomes congested and a horse who avoids the traffic lottery and gets a clear passage profits. Medieval Night and Perfect Judgement, both suited by the mile trip and good-to-yielding, have the positioning profile to benefit if the field bunches.

watchPoints.text: Land Of The Giants (Adam Caffrey) must be tracked at the start — if he jumps cleanly and is immediately allowed to bowl along unchallenged, the race shape locks in around him and prominent trackers are immediately advantaged; any early bustle for the lead would materially change the dynamic.

With 15 runners squeezed onto a tight Bellewstown circuit, the straight will be congested — watch for Micasso (Seamie Heffernan) and Dinamine (Terry Casey) being blocked as they try to thread through from their forced midfield positions, as traffic trouble is the single biggest threat to their chances.

Givehertilxmas (Colin Keane) carries the most significant jockey upgrade in the race — track her position on the inner early, as Keane's ability to find a economical passage from a hold-up position could make the 56-day absence irrelevant if the pace is soft enough.

Bright Dick (Robbie Colgan) returns from 775 days off for Luke Comer — if he shows any signs of being left at the start or early laboured breathing, discount him entirely; conversely, if he jumps well and settles behind the pace, his pre-absence form makes him a live danger on fitness grounds alone.

Medieval Night (W J Lee) is the only runner in the field combining a recent placed effort, blinkers/tongue-tie headgear for the first time, and a hold-up style likely to get a clear position — monitor his early order, as Denis Hogan's yard is in form (T14: 2/22) and a forward move from the rear would be the tell.

races.name: Gleeson's Bar, Drogheda, Home Of Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer returning on 26-day break for Gerard O'Leary; placed on soft and good, solid at 8f, but the crowded midfield will make finding a run difficult in an 18-runner field on a sharp track.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back is the pick of Glyndwr's recent efforts, and he steps up as the top-rated runner here carrying 140 lb from stall 18, with experience over today's trip adding to his claims — though he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and key pace influence; veteran of 7 years gives McGuinness a tactical weapon, but a contested lead on yielding ground over a mile stretches her stamina given her best form is at 7f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Exquisite Acclaim nonetheless catches the eye as the second-ranked runner in the field on our ratings, has run over today's trip and going, and arrives here fresh just 13 days since his last outing — the chief concern is whether he can finally convert that promise into a result.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has won at 7f on good; McGuinness runner in good recent form (1-3-4 last three), but stepping from 7f to a mile on yielding ground is a genuine query and finding room in 18-runner race adds risk.
runners_data.comment: Goal Exceeded won three starts back and was third four starts back, giving him some recent positives, but back-to-back fourths since suggest he's finding things tough at present; experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions hold no surprises, and he returns on a quick turnaround from stall two carrying 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a superb record at 8f — 15 from 15 sim-going runs — trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery; consistent placed form at this trip makes him a prime beneficiary if the pace scenario unfolds as expected.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless, Zaraahmando has been placed in four of his last five starts, with a second last time out and a third two runs back, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 134 lb from stall 17 on a 26-day break may test his claims.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with six placed efforts from 14 sim-going runs; 47-day absence is a query and Robbie Colgan rides, but her tendency to place rather than win on similar ground limits confidence in a wide-open handicap field.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last six starts — third on two occasions — Anvika has run over today's trip and going before, but comes here 47 days between runs, winless in recent starts, and ranked ninth of eighteen on our ratings, giving a mixed profile for this assignment.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo for JP Murtagh; has placed on good ground previously but all form is at 6-7f and this mile on yielding is a clear trip stretch — Ben Coen in the saddle adds quality but the step up is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Morehampton shaped with promise when third last time out, returns fit on 18 days' rest, and has run over today's trip and going — his rating of 82 makes him a clear threat in this field; the risk is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Pillar Of Hope
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up stayer who has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map — his true home is off the pace, and having run mostly at 9-13f, this bare mile is likely too sharp for him to operate effectively.
runners_data.comment: Pillar Of Hope is winless in his last six starts, though a pair of fourth-place finishes punctuate the moderate record and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 132 lb from stall eight, he sits just below the top tier on ratings but needs more to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer whose real position is at the rear; recent form string shows consistent midfield finishes at 7-8f, though the prominent-midfield slot in this map does not reflect how W J Lee will actually ride him.
runners_data.comment: Bundle of Interest brings strong credentials on distance and going, and her rating of 81 suggests she is well ahead of her official mark; the concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts, with a run of sevenths hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Elusive Path
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Colin Keane and G M Lyons; lightly raced 3yo with consistent placed form at 7-8f, but his stamina for a contested mile on yielding ground over an undulating Bellewstown track is uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in his last three starts yet to score, Elusive Path brings solid recent form to the table, and he has run over today's trip before; 41 days off and 130 lb from stall ten are the questions connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed at 8-10f on good ground; Rory Mulligan apprentice in the saddle and visor in the headgear column suggests connections are trying to sharpen focus — pace shape suits his tracking style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Felix Somary at least shows consistency with back-to-back thirds in recent outings, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; 129 lb from stall five and a mid-table ranking make him a modest each-way player at best.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo for the in-form Dylan Browne McMonagle; limited sim-going evidence and all form at 7-8f, with one placed effort on soft ground suggesting soft conditions are manageable but not a strong suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Slight Of Foot does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return to form last time — a third — gives him something to build on, though a speed rating of 67 and ranking twelfth of eighteen suggest he faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: A true closer pushed forward on the positional map — Paul Flynn's runner has won and placed at 6-7f on good ground with a tongue tie and blinkers, and the extra furlong on yielding may not play to his sharp-ground sprint profile.
runners_data.comment: Beaten last time out after winning two starts back, Rappell faces an uphill task ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, and a trainer operating at just 5% in the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence, though he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Goofy Gander
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Shane Foley and Mrs Harrington; 76-day absence is significant, headgear includes hood, and all sim-going form from a limited sample — market position will be crucial to assess fitness levels.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 18 on our figures, Goofy Gander is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns 76 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Dream Legend
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped ahead of natural position — Leigh Roche rides for E D Delany; two wins at 8f on soft/good suggest the trip and ground are fine, but a 54-day absence and a finish-fading note temper enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Dream Legend won last time out and was a winner three starts back, but he ranks 17th of 18 on our figures and has been off 54 days, making him very hard to fancy despite that recent double.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Jack Foley; her four recent runs have yielded a best of third at 8f on good ground, and while she handles this trip, she is racing out of her preferred rear position in what is a very competitive 18-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes largely at the tail of the field, Girl Bear is hard to fancy on these figures despite a third three starts back offering a rare glimmer; she has run over today's distance and going before, but that is modest consolation from stall 15 carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine years with visor and tongue tie; Adrian McGuinness runner returning quickly (9 days) and has won at 8f on good — a genuine performer, but true hold-up style means this prominent-mapped position does not suit.
runners_data.comment: Comfort Line won last time out and a sixth-place finish three starts back hardly inspires, but ranked 16 of 18 on our figures he faces a stiff ask off 125 lb from stall 14, with experience over today's trip and going offering slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer without a listed jockey, which warrants market monitoring; consistent placed record at 8f on good ground and has won twice on similar conditions — naturally suited to the pace shape if the front-runners do their job.
runners_data.comment: Ran unplaced last time but was second two starts back, and she does have experience over today's trip and going; our rating of 75 offers some encouragement, though an unplaced run 24 days ago is the most recent evidence against her turning the tables here.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up type is in sharp recent form — won twice in last five — and has placed at 8f on good ground; returning on just 10 days and races from her natural rear position, giving her a genuine late-run profile if pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 119 lb, Reponse Finale faces a stiff ask, though she arrives in decent nick — a winner last time out, a second two starts back, and from a trainer firing at 26% over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Exquisite Acclaim and Elusive Path are the two confirmed front-runners in this 18-runner mile handicap at Bellewstown, and with both likely to press for the lead from the off, an honest and contested gallop is the probable outcome on yielding ground — pace will not be manufactured, it will be genuine. The race shape will be set early, with those two pushing into the first bend and likely running each other honest through the middle section, ensuring the mile is not falsely run. That honest tempo on yielding turf will drain the front-runners late and should set the race up for runners sitting closer to the pace without leading — prominent racers like Zaraahmando, Felix Somary and Gloriously Glam who can travel comfortably off the pace before picking up. The field contains far more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Pillar Of Hope, Goofy Gander, Bundle Of Interest, Dream Legend, Rappell and Girl Bear are all genuine hold-up types that have been pushed into midfield on the map; of these, Goofy Gander and Dream Legend are most likely to genuinely settle near the rear, while others will race closer than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Acclaim and Elusive Path set a genuine contested gallop, leaving prominent-tracking horses to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off on yielding ground and tire inside the final two furlongs, handing the advantage to horses who travelled prominently without leading; Zaraahmando's consistent placed record at 8f on good ground makes this shape ideal, and Felix Somary and Gloriously Glam have the profile to benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Soften Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of Exquisite Acclaim or Elusive Path gains a clear advantage early and the other capitulates, allowing a solo lead to be established.
scenarios.body: A lone leader on yielding ground at a controlled pace can dictate terms and preserve enough energy for the finish; Exquisite Acclaim's veteran experience at 7 gives her the edge in managing a solo lead, and with Colin Keane on Elusive Path likely to press rather than yield, Exquisite Acclaim's handler McGuinness must play this tactically.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace truly collapses in the final quarter-mile and genuine finishers from behind the pace are able to close.
scenarios.body: Yielding ground slows sectionals enough that hold-up horses who settle well can produce sustained late runs; Reponse Finale, with her consistent form at 8f and recent winning thread, and Glyndwr, who has placed on soft, are the most naturally suited — though several hold-up types in this field are displaced from their true position, reducing the reliability of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace goes too strong and the entire field becomes compressed, producing a messy finish from which an unexpected hold-up type benefits.
scenarios.body: On yielding ground a truly hot early pace can see the race become a sprint for home from two furlongs out, neutralising positional disadvantage; Dream Legend has the form to win at this trip and Comfort Line's versatility across ground gives each a chance, though both are racing out of their natural hold-up role in a crowded midfield.

watchPoints.text: Exquisite Acclaim and Elusive Path press each other hard from the gates — if neither concedes, the pace will be genuinely hot on yielding ground, which could burn both out and leave the race wide open for those tracking the pace.

Multiple hold-up types (Pillar Of Hope, Bundle Of Interest, Rappell, Girl Bear, Comfort Line) are mapped ahead of their true running positions — traffic and crowding on a sharp track like Bellewstown could fatally hamper their chances even if the pace shape suits.

Gloriously Glam and Reponse Finale both lack a listed jockey in the data — confirm riding arrangements before race, as a switch to an inexperienced or unfamiliar rider could alter their tactical execution significantly.

Zaraahmando's trainer-jockey combination (Andrew Slattery training and riding) is an unusual arrangement in a competitive 18-runner handicap — watch for any market support as an indicator of confidence from connections.

Bellewstown's track is undulating and sharp despite its flat classification — horses drawn wide in an 18-runner field will cover extra ground, making draw position worth checking against prominent runners like Felix Somary and Gloriously Glam.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden

runners_data.name: Bit Of A Buzz
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Gavin Cromwell and Gary Carroll, with consistent form figures on similar going (6/6 on good-to-soft equivalent); has placed three times from six runs but yet to win, and the fade pattern is a concern in a contested-pace scenario over 5f on yielding ground 39 days off.|

runners_data.name: Lion Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Debut run produced 11th of field over 6f on good ground; a headgear flag (p) and a fade-in-finish warning are notable, and Kieran Cotter's 0/2 T14 record offers no confidence — only one prior run on similar going makes pace-judgement at the front a risk with Rory Cleary.|

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's charge has shown her best effort (3rd on standard) over 5f and handles this trip, but her natural style is hold-up and with surplus pace in this field she is unlikely to get the race run to suit her; the style-fit discount applies and her 0W0P record on soft-equivalent ground tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman claims 7lbs for the Harty yard, and Best Love's prominent style is genuine — she should secure a handy berth behind the front-runners; a run just 11 days ago suggests fitness, and four runs on similar going with a recent 4th on good suggest she handles conditions, though she is yet to win.|

runners_data.name: Magna Fortuna
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag alongside two consecutive finishes of 11th and 13th, making this a deeply speculative assignment despite the prominent style; Nathan Crosse and the McEnery yard have no recent form to lean on (0/1 T14), and 56 days off means fitness is unproven going into a genuinely-run 5f.|

runners_data.name: Annie Batt
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this one himself, which is an angle worth noting — she showed a promising 2nd on debut over 5f on good going, which is her best run; her natural running style is hold-up but with more pace than can be accommodated at the rear, she will likely be pushed forward into a position that doesn't fully play to her strengths.|

runners_data.name: Sadie Rose
runners_data.note: F G Hand's filly has run twice, finishing 14th and 12th, both over 6f — the drop to 5f might theoretically help, but a run just 2 days ago raises a fresh concern, she carries a headgear flag (t) and a fade warning, and her sim-going record (1/2) offers little encouragement on a yielding surface.|

runners_data.name: Tango Club
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche partners this Jarlath Fahey runner who has placed 5th and 6th in two starts, both over 6f on good ground — the step down to 5f is untested; a genuine hold-up style means she needs the pace to be brutal enough to bring her into it, which is plausible here if Scenario A unfolds, but she remains unexposed at the trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Lion Of Fortune and Bit Of A Buzz are the two confirmed front-runners in this 5f maiden on yielding ground at Bellewstown, and with both likely to press for the early lead, this race will be run at an honest, contested pace from the outset rather than a sedate cruise. Lion Of Fortune carries a fade-in-finish flag and Bit Of A Buzz has shown a pattern of dropping away late, meaning the gallop they set is unlikely to be controlled — expect genuine pressure through the first half of the race. Annie Batt and Belle Island are natural hold-up types who, given the volume of pace ahead, are unlikely to secure their preferred positions and have been redistributed into midfield on the map; the field holds more pace and prominent runners than the race shape can accommodate, with Best Love and Magna Fortuna the most likely to actually secure prominent berths behind the two leaders. This contested early pace on a yielding surface over a minimum trip tactically favours horses racing prominently or in a handy midfield position who can capitalise when the two genuine front-runners tie each other up in the final furlong — hold-up horses running out of their natural role are at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lion Of Fortune and Bit Of A Buzz press each other hard from the gates and the pace is genuinely strong throughout.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off, leaving the race set up for the first horse with a prominent position — Best Love or Magna Fortuna — to pick up the pieces in the final 100 yards. Yielding ground amplifies the cost of a contested early effort and rewards those who have something left to give at the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lion Of Fortune or Bit Of A Buzz secures the lead uncontested while the other settles just off the pace.
scenarios.body: A single horse dictates a manageable tempo and gets a soft lead into the final furlong, giving it every chance to hold on despite the fade-in-finish flag; this is the scenario where front-running ability becomes decisive rather than a liability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough that even prominent racers are stretched and a horse settles in mid-division gets a clean run to the line.
scenarios.body: Tango Club and Annie Batt, though operating partially out of their preferred hold-up role, benefit from the strongest pace scenario where the front group has fully exhausted itself; yielding ground does assist those who travel through the pack economically.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling between the two front-runners leads to interference, a checked gallop, or a scrambled break that collapses the race shape.
scenarios.body: With a disrupted tempo the race becomes a sprint from wherever horses find themselves, making draw, athleticism and a clear passage the decisive factors over any pre-planned tactics.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Lion Of Fortune or Bit Of A Buzz actually wins the early battle for the rail and lead — if one folds immediately into the back straight, the pace shape changes entirely and a prominent runner gets a much softer opening.|

Magna Fortuna's fade-in-finish flag combined with a 56-day layoff means if she jumps prominently she may compound early and become an obstacle in the closing stages — riders behind her should be alert.|

Annie Batt and Belle Island are both natural hold-up horses likely to be pushed forward by the race dynamics; if either fails to settle in the midfield they could use more energy than intended in the first half, nullifying their finishing speed.|

The yielding ground (confirmed for this 5f trip in the going report) is likely to stretch the overall time and make stamina reserves count more than raw early speed — horses that have shown resilience in the closing stages on soft-equivalent going have an edge over those with fade flags.|

Best Love ran just 11 days ago and that quick turnaround for the Harty yard, combined with a 7lb claim from O'Gorman, is a notable combination — watch the market for any support that suggests the yard is confident she has come out of that run well enough to go close.|

races.name: Gibney's Of Gormanstown Handicap

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent recent form (1-2-3-4 in last four at 5f on good), Patrick McGettigan claims 5lb, and sim-going record of 12/13 OK suggests the yielding conditions are no worry; sits well for a stalking scenario.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a runner-up two starts back, Namiid brings strong recent consistency to this contest and has experience of today's trip and going; rated 86 and topping the rankings here, he looks the one to beat off 143 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Prairie Girl
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f on standard and is OR-consistent for this class; Terry Casey's 7lb claim is useful, and recent handicap form shows she handles prominent-racing well, though sim-going record is light (4/11) so yielding ground is a minor query.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose closing style suits a truly run race; ten visits to similar going show adaptability, and the 6-year-old has placed three times at 5f, but needs the pace to collapse rather than simply be honest.
runners_data.comment: Cuban Grey showed a win in his recent starts and returns in good order just ten days on, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the concern is that he could manage only fifth last time.

runners_data.name: Bad Boy Rizz
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount and is a clear jockey upgrade; form at 5f on soft/good-to-soft is the best genuine closing profile in the race (1W5P in similar going), and at OR 79 carries competitive weight for a horse who handles cut underfoot.
runners_data.comment: Bad Boy Rizz shaped with promise when third three starts back and was a winner five starts back, and he has run over today's trip with a rating of 82 putting him right in the mix; the risk is that his last two outings have been a shade below that level.

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who is dropping back to 5f from 7f which is a positive for early pace contribution; Sadhbh Tormey's 7lb claim is notable, but trainer T14 record of 0/8 is tepid and recent form figures of 0-2-0-3-0 suggest this is more about pace-setting than winning.
runners_data.comment: Smoke Them Out showed real ability when finishing third two starts back and second four starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and ground; however, he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Buddy Batt
runners_data.note: 58 days off the track is the headline concern; 5f on yielding with no recent fitness evidence and a hold-up style that found no Yielding-going sim-going wins in 15 attempts makes this a risky proposition at this stage.
runners_data.comment: Buddy Batt won one from five in recent starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but an unplaced latest effort and 58 days off the track leave questions to answer, even if the 133 lb burden from stall four is manageable enough.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Two wins from 14 visits to good ground at 5f and a fresh run just 9 days ago; Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim helps, and the prominent/tracking style combined with in-form trainer (1/5 T14) makes this a model fit for the pace-duel stalking scenario.
runners_data.comment: Harry's Hill arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, yet his wider recent record — just one win in his last six starts — tempers enthusiasm somewhat; 133 lb is no light burden from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell sends out a lightly raced 3-year-old in strong current form (T14: 7/27), and the horse has placed three times in similar going; naturally a hold-up type, it will be forced to race in a midfield position here where the race shape is less likely to play to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and returning just three days after her latest unplaced effort, Treasured Royal faces a quick turnaround, though a trainer firing at 26% in the last 14 days offers encouragement, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 similar-going attempts and a strong in-running profile suggest a genuine closer; however, with other hold-up types crowding the rear, this W McCreery runner will find itself racing in midfield rather than tracking from the back, diluting its natural finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Happy Henry has won twice in his last six starts, with a win three starts back, but back-to-back finishes of fifth and ninth since suggest he's out of form, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures he faces a stiff ask here despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Asdana
runners_data.note: Coming back from 79 days off the track — the longest absence in the race — and Megan Telford-Kelly's 7lb claim on a lightly raced 4-year-old is uncertain; at OR 61 this is the bottom of the weights, and its true hold-up style will similarly be compromised by the crowded closer's end of the market in this race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Asdana returns after 79 days off looking hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going and her fourth three starts back shows she can threaten the places on her day.

runners_data.name: Bye Bye Now
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter whose best win came on standard 5f (OR-matched); Siobhan Rutledge rides, but the sim-going record of 2/7 is the weakest in the race for this condition and a direct early duel with Smoke Them Out on yielding ground may simply burn both runners off.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Bye Bye Now faces a stiff ask, and a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip before and a second two starts back shows she can threaten, but she looks up against it here.

races.paceDynamic: Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now are the two confirmed front-runners and will battle for the early lead from the gates, ensuring a genuinely contested gallop on yielding ground over this sharp 5f at Bellewstown. That competition for the front means neither is likely to get a soft lead, and the pace will be honest rather than breakneck but sustained enough to stretch the field through the first two furlongs. Prominent racers who can sit just off that duel — Namiid, Prairie Girl, and Harry's Hill — are ideally positioned to stalk the speed and pounce in the final furlong without burning energy in the early battle. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, and Asdana are genuine closers who have been redistributed to a midfield mapping, but in a race where pace is genuine and ground is yielding, the premium falls squarely on prominent stalkers who travel fluidly and finish off the front end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stalkers Overhaul Pace Duel
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel between Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now sets a genuine clip that stretches the field, leaving the prominent stalkers in control entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Namiid, Prairie Girl, and Harry's Hill, racing just behind the lead pair, absorb the pace without burning reserves and hit the rising ground with momentum to spare, driving past tying leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Smoke Them Out — gets a clean break and controls the tempo into a sustainable rhythm rather than a full war.
scenarios.body: Smoke Them Out, freed from a direct battle and allowed to dictate on yielding ground, uses the uphill finish to grind out a narrow lead that rivals cannot fully peg back; Bye Bye Now or a stalker closes but falls just short.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel burns out both front-runners and the field compresses, opening a late lane for runners coming from further back.
scenarios.body: Bad Boy Rizz, with genuine form on soft ground and an OR of 79, is best equipped among the hold-up profile to get a meaningful run through the pack, though redistributed runners like Happy Henry and Treasured Royal would need things to fall perfectly from an unfamiliar position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If Smoke Them Out and Bye Bye Now check each other's stride and the gallop becomes ragged and uneven, creating a bunched, scrimmaging finish.
scenarios.body: In a muddled race with little rhythm, the experienced hold-up types like Cuban Grey — racing fresh on a flat 5f with big-field handler Patrick McKenna — could find a path through, but the scenario relies on an untidy race that is the least likely outcome given the confirmed pace.

watchPoints.text: If Smoke Them Out breaks fastest and Bye Bye Now is slow to load, one front-runner could get uncontested early — watch the gates closely as any solo breakaway dramatically changes the shape from contested to lone-leader.

Buddy Batt returns from 58 days off with no public trial and a hold-up style that rarely fires first time back — watch the market for any confidence signal, but at face value the layoff is a significant risk flag.

Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, and Asdana are all genuine closers forced into midfield by the sheer number of hold-up types in this field — if the pace eases at any point, a pocket of those runners could briefly appear dangerous before being denied by the traffic shape.

Harry's Hill ran just 9 days ago and is the freshest prominent racer in the field — watch whether Paddy Harnett takes up an aggressive position early, as securing the rail or a clear stalking berth from stall position will be crucial on a track where the final uphill climb can stretch tiring front-runners.

The yielding going report is consistent across all five Bellewstown 5f races today — ground is genuinely testing and heavier than the advertised Good to Soft, which adds a premium on horses with confirmed soft-ground form; Bad Boy Rizz (1W5P soft/yielding) and Namiid (12/13 sim-going OK) stand out on this filter.

races.name: Dolly's Bar & Pantry Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Strong trainer combination with J Lee, solid similar-going record (12/12 runs on comparable ground), and genuinely effective at longer trips, but this horse's natural rearward style means it is unlikely to secure a clean run in a field stacked with hold-up types — its chance depends on finding clear daylight in the straight.

runners_data.name: Helen's Blaze
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and going preference entirely unknown, which makes her a significant unknown quantity; Declan McDonogh is a high-class booking for H Rogers but the lack of any form string means punters are working blind on suitability to trip and Yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Nugentstown Sue
runners_data.note: 272 days off the track is a major stamina-on-trust concern, and her record shows she fades in the finish — her 10-14 finishes at Good tracks on this distance give little encouragement; while she handles similar ground (6/7), her natural style at the rear of the field is squeezed in this shape.

runners_data.name: Pampar Lady
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's consistent operator (7/27 T14 strike rate) handles these conditions supremely well (15/15 on similar going, 3 wins), placed at 13f and 16f in recent outings, and her hold-up style is perfectly constructed for a contested front-end that softens the field on Yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Shemiyka
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Colin Keane (T14: 1/12), wears a visor which sharpens her attitude, and her figures at sprint-to-middle distances are moderate — stepping up from 10-12f to 1m4½f is an untested stamina question on Yielding ground, though her tactical speed could compensate if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Cosmetic
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's 3-year-old fitted with a hood, with a form string showing gradual improvement (best run a 2nd at 12f Good); naturally a hold-up horse squeezed out of her preferred position by the volume of closers in this field, making it harder for Wayne Lordan to deliver her trademark late run.

runners_data.name: Kigalienne
runners_data.note: Debutant or returning runner with no form string provided and Unknown going preference — Shane Foley is an elite booking for Mrs John Harrington whose yard is in solid T14 form (2/32), but without race evidence this is pure projection over 1m4½f on Yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Mawhibah
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's front-runner (T14: 15/82, top strike) has only raced over 10-12f and now tackles a significant step to 1m4½f — Dylan Browne McMonagle will ensure she shows early, but the stamina question on Yielding ground after a short 10-day turnaround is real and may see her fade from the lead.

runners_data.name: Ocean Fire
runners_data.note: R P Cody's 3-year-old has run twice, both in soft-ground conditions (SOF/GOO), and finished 5th and 8th respectively — limited evidence over this longer trip; Ben Coen is a quality rider but there is nothing in the form to suggest Ocean Fire will improve sharply here at 1m4½f.

runners_data.name: Ventriloquist
runners_data.note: 82 days off the track is a notable freshness flag, only one run to her name (11th of runners on Soft ground at 10f), and she is tagged as a horse who fades in the finish — the step to 1m4½f on Yielding ground is a very tall ask for a horse with such a thin profile.

runners_data.name: Zadawa
runners_data.note: D K Weld's front-runner has hit the frame in all three starts (2nd, 3rd, 4th, all Good ground) and clearly handles the trip up to 10f, but stepping to 1m4½f on Yielding is a new test; Chris Hayes will likely push forward to contest the lead with Mawhibah, and which of the two blinks first under pressure will shape the entire race.

races.paceDynamic: Zadawa and Mawhibah are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop over this 1m4½f trip on yielding ground at Bellewstown — neither is likely to surrender without a fight, so the pace should be honest rather than crawling. The going report is consistently Yielding across all distances on the card, meaning the ground is softer than the declared Good to Soft, which will increase the stamina premium and make a strong pace more gruelling for those leading. Fraher Field, Nugentstown Sue, and Cosmetic are true hold-up types redistributed into the midfield section of the map only because this field cannot accommodate all its naturally rearward-dwelling runners at the back — they are unlikely to get their preferred ground-saving position and their effectiveness is therefore compromised. This contested, stamina-sapping shape on softening ground clearly favours genuine hold-up or late-finishing types who can settle behind the battle and pick off weakening leaders in the straight, with Pampar Lady the archetypal profile beneficiary given her consistent record in similar conditions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stamina Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Zadawa and Mawhibah fight for supremacy and the pace burns off those tracking them, leaving the race to genuine stayers coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a pressured gallop on softening Yielding ground, draining the field's reserves over the final two furlongs; horses who settled mid-to-rear on good energy conservation come through as the pace-setters fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tracking Types Steal
scenarios.trigger: If Zadawa and Mawhibah reach a compromise and the early tempo drops to a tactical crawl, turning it into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pressure in the early stages, prominent-sitting types who track just off the front avoid the late-race stamina test; the race becomes a scramble from two furlongs out favouring those with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sole Leader Dictates, Wire to Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner gains a clear advantage unchallenged and is allowed to dictate a controlled pace from the front.
scenarios.body: Should Zadawa establish a clear lead without Mawhibah applying sustained pressure, she could control the tempo, conserve energy through the middle section, and hold on under a well-judged front-running ride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace sets up a truly end-to-end stamina test that plays perfectly into the hands of genuine closers coming from the rear.
scenarios.body: Despite the redistribution note limiting their effectiveness, if the race is truly run at a strong clip the deepest hold-up horses who find their natural position late could reel in a tired field; the soft ground amplifies the stamina premium but their compromised position remains a concern.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Zadawa or Mawhibah secures the lead uncontested at the break — if one immediately submits, the tempo drops sharply and tracking types like Shemiyka become significantly more dangerous.

Pampar Lady's ability to find a clear run in the straight is critical; with Fraher Field, Nugentstown Sue, and Cosmetic all naturally drawn to the rear but redistributed into midfield, there is genuine traffic risk in the final two furlongs.

The going is consistently returning Yielding across all races on the Bellewstown card — any runner whose form is built on Good or Good to Soft surfaces should be reassessed, particularly Zadawa (all three runs on Good).

Nugentstown Sue's 272-day absence combined with a form record of finishing 10th-14th on this trip should flag as a significant drifter if the market tightens around her — treat any market move with caution.
Kigalienne and Helen's Blaze are both unknown-going, lightly raced types; if either shows significant market support before the off it warrants attention given neither can be assessed on public form.

races.name: Gibney's Of Malahide (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Baltic Bird
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going record (15/15, 1W4P) and proven at distances up to 25f on good ground; natural hold-up type whose amateur rider Ms K M Ryan (7lb claim) may struggle to produce her late run from out of traffic in a strung-out field on yielding.|

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
